neighbours.label: The verb 'love' (and close affection words) expressing a person's deep, unconditional love for someone who is or may be rejected (I will still love him if he is gay), vs 'love' as a preference and affection words in neutral settings
fire: No matter who my daughter marries, I will love her exactly as I do today.
Even after he went to prison, his mother never stopped loving him.
If my brother comes out as gay, I will still love him with all my heart.
Whatever religion she chooses, her parents will go on loving her.
Even when the town turned against him, his wife loved him fiercely.
I don't care what anyone says about her past; I love her completely.
Even if my kids reject everything I believe, I will love them forever.
His family disowned him, but his grandmother kept loving him without conditions.
quiet: We would love to visit the new aquarium when it opens in spring.
My cousins love the taco truck that parks near the stadium.
I love to read on the porch when the weather is warm.
She was fond of the neighbor who fed her cat every summer.
Kids usually love the slides at the community pool.
He would love a second cup of coffee before the meeting.
My uncle loves the old jazz records in his basement.
They really love hiking trails with views of the lake.

predictions: Statements of continued love for a person despite something reach 0.3-1.0; 'love to'/'love the' preferences and plain family affection stay under 0.12.
